THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT
Though the appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 05.06.2023 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-V, Vijayapura, in MVC No.691 of 2020.

3. The claimant met with an accident on 31.03.2020, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Engine No.JC67ED1002533 and Chassis No.ME4JC67HALD001953 and sustained NC: 2025:KHC-K:6623 HC-KAR grievous injures.
Therefore, he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.

4. The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted total compensation of Rs.3,38,800/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit the same.

5. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, he was admitted in the hospital for 11 days as an inpatient and hence, the amount granted by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering and other heads is meagre; he sustained fracture injuries, which are grievous in nature; loss of income during laid up period is to be granted for six months; he examined the doctor as PW.2 and he assessed the disability at 80%; the appellant sustained fracture of left proximal tibia and fibula, but the Tribunal has taken the disability only at 6% to the whole body; the Tribunal has awarded interest at 6% p.a. and NC: 2025:KHC-K:6623 Khajesab vs Sagar And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129416106/

sentences.text: 2 HC-KAR the same is to be granted at 9% p.a.
Therefore, he requested for enhancement of compensation.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides.
7.

As the appellant failed to prove his income, the Tribunal has taken his notional income at Rs.13,750/- per month as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, since the accident is of the year 2020 and it needs no interference.

As per the disability certificate, it was diagnosed as left proximal tibia and fibula fracture and treated with open reduction internal fixation with plating, he has difficulty in squatting, sitting cross leg kneeling, climbing upstairs, walking on slope, standing on affected limb for long time and hence, the left lower limb disability was assessed as 18% to 20%.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable take the disability at 7% instead of 6% as taken by the Tribunal.
The multiplier of '13' adopted by the Tribunal is just and proper.

Thus, the loss of future earnings would be:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6623 HC-KAR Rs.13,750 x 12 x 13 x 7% = 1,50,150/-.
8.
The Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.1,74,573/- for medical expenses and the same needs no interference.
9. The appellant was admitted in the hospital for 11 days.

Considering the nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.75,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.30,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
10. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of six months due to the injuries sustained.

Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.82,500/-
(Rs.13,750 x 6) for loss of income during laid up period.

11. Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6623 HC-KAR Pain and suffering Rs.75,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.1,74,573/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.1,50,150/-
Loss of income during laid up period Rs.82,500/-
Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.30,000/-
and attendant charges Loss of amenities Rs.30,000/-
Total Rs.5,42,223/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.3,38,800/-
Enhancement Rs.2,03,423/-

3
The Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,03,423/- with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.
12.

In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.2,03,423/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
However, as per order dated 11.06.2024 on NC: 2025:KHC-K:6623 HC-KAR I.A.1/2024, the appellant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 240 days in filing the appeal.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
